svg.title: The Listed Surplus Is Not the Owner's Remainder
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-competing-debt-allocation; chapter number: 4; title: The Listed Surplus Is Not the Owner's Remainder; subtitle: Alfred Taren's worked example reduces $180,000 to $55,000 after competing debt.; caption: Alfred Taren illustrates a $95,000 second mortgage, $8,000 HOA debt, and $22,000 judgment against a $180,000 listed surplus.; assumptions note: Taren gives fixed illustrative amounts, not low and high estimates. Equal bounds preserve those amounts without introducing an unsupported range.; note: Taren advises checking what the actual case or sale file has already paid and keeping owner-facing amounts estimated. The $55,000 remainder is not a promised payment or a stated net amount after recovery fees.; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: $180,000 illustrated listed surplus; buckets: label: Second mortgage; low: 95000; high: 95000; notes: Taren's illustrated competing mortgage deduction.; label: HOA debt; low: 8000; high: 8000; notes: Taren's illustrated homeowners association deduction.; label: Judgment; low: 22000; high: 22000; notes: Taren's illustrated judgment deduction.; label: Illustrated remainder; low: 55000; high: 55000; notes: Taren's reported remainder after the listed deductions; not an established claimant payout.
